title: Light and Darkness Theme
summary: Light and darkness do different work across these passages. Genesis 1:1–5 introduces light as God orders creation; Psalm 27:1 calls the LORD “my light and my salvation”; John 1:1–9 presents life and light in the Word; Ephesians 5:8–14 turns the image into an ethical call to live as children of light; and 1 John 1:5–10 connects walking in the light with truth, fellowship, and confession. The theme moves from creation and trust to moral life and honest relationship with God.
historical_context: The passages use the light image in distinct settings. Genesis 1 places light in the creation account. Psalm 27 uses it in a prayer of confidence amid danger. John 1 opens with language about the beginning, life, and light, inviting readers to compare its imagery with Genesis without requiring every detail to have the same meaning. Ephesians 5 addresses the conduct of a Christian community, while 1 John 1 contrasts walking in light with denying sin. These settings help distinguish creation imagery, personal trust, and ethical instruction.
literary_context: Genesis 1 tells of light appearing at the beginning of creation; Psalm 27 uses light as a compact image of safety and salvation; John 1 brings together beginning, life, and light; Ephesians 5 contrasts darkness with the “fruit of light” and calls for wakefulness; and 1 John 1 pairs light with truth, fellowship, and confession. The images overlap, but they are not interchangeable: one passage orders creation, another voices trust, and the later texts connect light with the Word and with truthful conduct.
covenantal_significance: The light imagery links trust in God with the way people live together. Psalm 27 presents God as the source of confidence; Ephesians 5 calls its readers to leave harmful conduct and practice what is good, right, and true; and 1 John 1 insists that fellowship with God cannot be separated from truth about sin. John 1 gives the image a distinctive focus in the life and light of the Word. Read alongside Genesis, these passages connect creation, revelation, and ethical response without reducing them to one metaphor.
canonical_role: Light and Darkness Theme serves as a thematic anchor, connecting repeated biblical patterns, key passages, and related theological concepts across the canon.

interpretive_notes.note: Read Light and Darkness Theme in its immediate context before generalizing.
Do not flatten distinct passages into one slogan; let the canon keep its own shape.
